content.text: Fixed and verified. **The change** — `render.py:8`, one line: ```python return text.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">") ``` **The part that mattered.** The obvious patch is to append `.replace("&", "&")` to the end of the existing chain. That is wrong, and the docstring already sitting above the function says why: escaping `&` last rewrites the ampersands that `<` and `>` just introduced, so `` renders to the user as a literal `<b>`. The existing `test_escapes_angle_brackets` catches that, which is why it was worth running the suite before touching anything — all 3 tests passed beforehand, confirming they did not cover the reported bug. **What I ran:** - Suite before the edit: 3 passed — so no existing test covered ampersands. - After adding 3 tests, before the fix: 3 failed, 3 passed. Each failure was the raw `&` passing through, not an import or setup error. - After the fix: 6 passed. - Cross-checked the output against stdlib `html.escape(s, quote=False)` on five inputs including ` & ` and the pre-escaped `&` — exact match on all. **Tests added** (`test_render.py`): the reported case `Tom & Jerry`; an ordering guard mixing `&` with tags, which fails if someone later re-appends the `&` replacement; and `&` → `&`, pinning down that input is treated as text, so a literal `&` a user types stays visible rather than decoding to a bare `&`. **Not covered:** `render()` escapes `<`, `>`, `&` but not quotes, so it is safe for element text but not for an unquoted or single-quoted attribute value — `render(x)` inside `` can still be broken out of. The repo has no callers of `render()` besides the test, so nothing is currently exposed, and adding `"` / `'` escaping is beyond the bug you reported. Worth knowing before the first attribute-context caller lands.
